//: Deploy with: firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes  (or: node deploy-indexes.mjs)

indexes.//2: Firestore appends the inequality field to the sort using the direction of the last explicit orderBy, hence userId DESCENDING.

indexes.//: startInterviewSession -> findResumableSession: where(userId ==).where(interviewId ==).where(status ==). Without it the reuse lookup falls back to an unindexed read, and a failed lookup would charge a second interview credit for one retried attempt.

//feedback: getFeedbackByInterviewId is where(interviewId ==).where(userId ==) with no orderBy. Firestore serves equality-only queries by merging the automatic single-field indexes, so no composite index is required. Verified against the live project: that query succeeds while the two above raise FAILED_PRECONDITION. A composite index here was removed rather than left in to avoid paying write amplification for an index nothing needs.
